steps.text: This chain can't lie completely flat and still be linked. Two rings lying flat in parallel planes can't pass through each other's holes. Each link has to stand at an angle to its neighbor, so the choice is how to lay the links out on the bed.

args.title: Chain layout
args.question: Links that interlock must stand at 90 degrees to their neighbors. Which layout should I build?

steps.text:
You said to use common sizes and sensible defaults, so I'll build it. Upright links interlock on the bed. Flat links can't, because a linked neighbor's wire has to pass through the hole at mid-height, above a flat link's bottom wire. So every link will stand on its edge and the chain lies on the bed as one piece.

Steps:
1. Plan the eight-link print-in-place chain (no approval needed).
2. Confirm the sizes on the sheet (no approval needed).
3. Build each link, then run the fit and plan checks (no approval needed).
4. Run the slice (no approval needed).
5. Send the plate to the P1S, which needs your OK.

assumptions: Outer link 30 mm long by 20 mm wide, 3 mm wire, inner opening 24 by 14 mm (common oval chain link).
Links alternate between the XZ and YZ planes so each one passes through its neighbor's opening; all stand on the bed.
Interlocked links keep at least 0.4 mm clearance where they meet.
Printed on the P1S with 0.4 mm nozzle, PLA; supports on the top bars of upright links.
